content.text:
Ownership belongs in `domain/models/funder_grouping.rs`. Policy currently owns reviewed family membership; `build_funder_groups` owns connected components and direct evidence. The component UUID is always its minimum persisted UUID. A preferred display name should be separate group metadata, determined after all alias and family joins, so it applies even when the representative is an alias-connected external identity.

The flow is:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[Reviewed policy and stored source names] --> B[build_funder_groups]
  B --> D[Atomic grouping projection]
  D --> S[Text and phonetic search]
  D --> F[Funder funding aggregate]
  F --> H[HTTP details response]
  H --> U[Summary and history header]
```

Name consumers:

- `outbound/funder.rs:63`: text search scores source names and aliases, then displays the representative's `funder_name`. Deduplication happens before the result limit.
- `outbound/funder.rs:154`: phonetic search follows the same pattern, restricted to individuals.
- Both searches calculate `matched_alias` using whether the winning identity differs from the representative. With preferred labels, a match on the representative's source name may also need provenance when its displayed name differs.
- `outbound/entity_details.rs:118`: funder details read the representative's name. They retain the requested funder UUID in the profile, even when it differs from the group UUID.
- `entity_details.rs:235`: funder history entries reuse that profile name.
- `domain/services/entity_details.rs:158`: summary calculation passes the profile through without choosing another name.
- HTTP handlers serialize these existing names unchanged. No response shape change is necessary.
- `frontend/src/SearchPage.svelte:344` renders the search name.
- `frontend/src/FunderIdentity.svelte:20` renders the shared summary/history heading.
- `frontend/src/MemberDeclarations.svelte:41` renders source identity names from the separate member-history query. Preserve this query's source-name behavior.
- Details aliases union all stored canonical names and aliases. Family evidence retains exact source names. These must remain unchanged.

Persistence currently stores memberships and evidence only. `outbound/funder_grouping.rs:37` refreshes them in one transaction, sharing the declaration loader advisory lock. Both explicit refresh and declaration ingestion call this projection. Add preferred metadata there without modifying `funders.funder_name` or creating source aliases.

Invariants and test targets:

- Minimum UUID and all memberships remain unchanged by display-name selection.
- Source funders, aliases, link evidence, funding counts and totals remain unchanged.
- Every member detail URL displays the same preferred label while retaining its requested UUID.
- Unreviewed groups retain the representative source-name fallback.
- A singleton reviewed source should receive its preferred label even though it produces no family link.
- A connected component touching multiple reviewed families needs explicit ambiguity behavior. Policy presently rejects duplicate reviewed normalized names, but aliases can bridge otherwise distinct families.
- Empty preferred values must fail at policy parsing.
- Text and phonetic output should consistently use preferred names while retaining source match provenance.
- Existing `reviewed_families_combine_all_names_and_preserve_distinct_evidence` in `outbound/funder.rs:553` inserts the desired labels with minimum UUIDs. Reverse that ordering to expose the present defect.
- Extend `connected_funding_preserves_entries_requested_id_and_link_evidence` in `outbound/entity_details/tests.rs:461` for preferred labels and unchanged source details.
- Domain grouping tests should cover input-order independence, singleton families, aliases making an external identity representative, fallback, malformed policy and family conflicts.
- Verify the reversible migration with existing source records and refresh twice.

One limitation to decide explicitly: merely changing output names does not add preferred names to search candidates. Current policies include preferred labels among reviewed source names, but a database containing only another family spelling may need preferred-name matching if searching the preferred label must always succeed.
